title: Rounding and Estimating: Number Lines and Compatible Numbers
seo_title: Grade 3 Rounding and Estimating Worksheets: Number Lines (TEKS 3.2C, 3.4B, STAAR)
standard_text: 3.2C represent a number on a number line as being between two consecutive multiples of 10; 100; 1,000; or 10,000 and use words to describe relative size of numbers in order to round whole numbers; 3.4B round to the nearest 10 or 100 or use compatible numbers to estimate solutions to addition and subtraction problems
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 rounding worksheets for Texas TEKS 3.2C and 3.4B: numbers between multiples on a number line, round to the nearest 10, 100, 1,000 and 10,000, estimate sums and differences, and word problems. 100 STAAR-style questions with answers.
key_big: Find the halfway point. Below it, round down. At it or above, round up.
key_sub: Look at the digit to the right of the rounding place: 0 to 4 round down, 5 to 9 round up.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Find the two multiples the number is between. 347 is between 300 and 400.
  • Find the halfway point (350). Below it, round down. At it or above, round up.
  • Short cut: look at the digit to the right of the place you round to. 0 to 4: round down. 5 to 9: round up.
  • To estimate, round each number first, then add or subtract. Compatible numbers like 25, 50 and 75 are easy to add.

Examples

Example

Estimate 486 + 231 by rounding to the nearest hundred.

486 is about 500.

231 is about 200.

500 + 200 = 700

Answer: about 700

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Rounding to the wrong placeUnderline the place you round to before you start.
Rounding 5 down5 or more rounds up: 350 rounds to 400.
Keeping the digits after the rounding place: 3,472 → 3,500 is right, 3,572 is notAll digits to the right become 0.

faq.a: Show a number on a number line between two multiples of 10, 100, 1,000 or 10,000, and use words to say which one it is closer to. This is how students learn to round.

faq.q: How do you round to the nearest hundred?
faq.a: Look at the tens digit. If it is 5 or more, round up. If it is less than 5, round down, and change the tens and ones to 0.
Numbers that are close to the real numbers and easy to work with in your head, like 25 + 75 or 250 + 150 (TEKS 3.4B).
An estimate tells you about how much and helps you check if an exact answer is reasonable.
